summary: Edward Joseph Thomas was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of St Andrews under John Burnet and at Cambridge. He served as Head and Librarian of the Cambridge University Library's Oriental Department and departmental Dean.

Edward Kamens worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Yale University from around 1974 to 1982, he served on its faculty from 1986 to 2022, becoming Sumitomo Professor Emeritus of East Asian Languages & Literatures.

Edward Klich worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Jagiellonian University around 1898 to 1902 under Jan Michał Rozwadowski, and became a professor at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań in 1929.
Edward Lavallin Puxley was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Brasenose College in 1852 and served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society from 1859 to 1866.

Edward Lucas Hogarth was an Indologist who studied at Brasenose College from 1859. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Oxford and served as Head Master at the Government Provincial School in Calicut.
Edward Payson Newton was an Indologist and linguist. He completed his studies at Princeton University (around 1866–1870) and Pittsburgh Theological Seminary (around 1870–1873).
Edward Peter Rice worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Cheshunt College and the University of London before serving with the London Missionary Society from 1873 to 1915.

Edward Rehatsek, trained in civil engineering at Eötvös Loránd University, worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He held professorships at the University of Breslau and Wilson College, Mumbai, and examined at the University of Mumbai.

Edward Ross works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and computational fields. He studied at McGill University, the University of Hong Kong, and the University of Reading, where he was appointed Associate Lecturer (2020–2025).

Edward Russell Ayrton worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at St Paul's School, he studied under Flinders Petrie, held a post at Abydos (~1902–1904), and succeeded Harry Charles Purvis Bell.

Philosopher Edward S. Casey studied at Yale, Northwestern, and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at Yale, UCSB, and Stony Brook University, where he was Dean of the Faculty of Philosophy, and presided over the APA (2009–2010).

Linguist Edward Sapir studied at Columbia University under Franz Boas and Wilhelm Wundt. He headed anthropology at the Geological Survey of Canada (1910–1925) and held professorships at the University of Chicago and Yale University.
Edward Thomas was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at East India Company College from around 1830 to 1832 and served as a writer in the Bengal Civil Service from 1832 to 1857.

Edward Upham was active in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Between roughly 1824 and 1834, he was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society and a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London.

Indologist and linguist Edward Vernon Arnold studied at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell and at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. A fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge, he served as professor at Bangor University from 1884 to 1924.

Edward W. Said studied at Victoria College, Northfield Mount Hermon School, Princeton University, and Harvard University. From around 1963 to 2003, he taught English and Comparative Literature at Columbia University.

Edward Washburn Hopkins, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Columbia and Leipzig under Ernst Windisch and Albrecht Weber. He taught at Columbia, served as professor at Bryn Mawr (1885–1895), and became professor at Yale in 1895.
Edward William West worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at King's College London, under Duncan Forbes, and was a disciple of Martin Haug between 1867 and 1873.

Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, receiving additional traditional training from Lobsang Tenzin, Geshe Lobsang, and Geshe Lobsang Donyo.

Linguist Edward Winter Clark studied at Worcester Academy, Brown University, Newton Theological Institution, and Colgate Rochester Crozer Divinity School. He served as a missionary with the American Baptist Missionary Union from 1869 to 1911.
